$comment: Single-sourced from concordance-semantic_protocol_service_scope.md §9.4. Declares the slots that POST /context-pack must populate when recipe='action_eligibility'. Mirrors the modify-ui-copy.json / debug-or-explain.json / semantic-location.json shape (per-slot derivation_rule, fail-loud loader). Sprint 11 m03 deliverable. The scope lists 10 nominal items (actor, actor role, object, object state, requested action, permission model, policy, side effects, safe alternatives, human explanation); per the s09-m03 #240 5-or-fewer-slot contract discipline these are distilled into 5 implementable slots that map cleanly onto the corpus shape (action entities have element.object + element.action + traits[] + outbound 'requires'/'depends_on'/'produces' edges; UI-button surfaces resolve to their triggered action via outbound 'triggers'). 'human explanation' is intentionally NOT a recipe slot — that surface is /explain (s06-m05 #154 separation: /context-pack returns structured slot data, /explain returns prose). 'actor' + 'actor role' fold into target_action.traits + target_action.pragmatic_role rather than separate slots. 'permission model' folds into preconditions + governing_policies. The 5-slot distillation matches the s10-m03 modify_ui_copy precedent and keeps the recipe discoverable.
description: Used for queries like 'Can support cancel this subscription?' or 'Can a customer retry payment after card was declined?' or 'May a buyer add this item to their cart?'. Resolves a UI-action surface (button/link) or an action entity, then returns the action identity, its preconditions (states/policies that must hold), governing policies (depends_on policies), expected effects (states it produces and objects it modifies), and safe alternative actions on the same object. Per s07-m02 ui-surface-wins-for-action_eligibility, the typical seed URN is a UI button; the slot builder walks outbound 'triggers' to find the underlying action and reads its outbound graph for the structural slots.

slots.name: target_action
slots.derivation_rule: If entity.element.type == 'action', return {urn, name, kind, pragmatic_role, traits, object, action} for the entity itself — the canonical action identification slot. If entity.element.type starts with 'ui.' (any ui.control.*, ui.notification.*, ui.layout.*), walk the outbound 'triggers' edge from the seed and return the same shape for the triggered action-kind target (covers the s07-m02 ui-surface-wins-for-action_eligibility pattern where benchmark queries hit a button URN whose action is one hop away). If neither path applies — seed is a state, policy, or non-action object — return MissingSlot with the actual kind in the reason. Resolution determines downstream slot derivation: preconditions / governing_policies / expected_effects / safe_alternatives all key off the resolved action's URN, not the seed's, when seed != action.

slots.name: preconditions
slots.derivation_rule: List of {urn, name, kind, edge_type, direction} entries naming entities the resolved action depends on as preconditions. Walk outbound 'requires' edges from target_action.urn (NOT the seed URN; corpus encodes 'action requires state' for lifecycle preconditions and 'action requires policy' for permission preconditions). Include both state-kind targets (lifecycle conditions like state-card-declined) and policy-kind targets (permission/governance conditions). direction='out_requires'. Deduplicate by urn (first encounter wins). Truncate to first 5 entries. Missing if target_action is itself MissingSlot OR if the resolved action has no outbound 'requires' edges (action with no encoded preconditions in the catalog).

slots.name: governing_policies
slots.derivation_rule: List of {urn, name, kind, edge_type, direction} policy entries that govern the resolved action via 'depends_on' edges (the corpus's policy-binding pattern, mirrors the modify_ui_copy content_constraints depends_on→policy path). Walk outbound 'depends_on' edges from target_action.urn and filter to targets where target.element.type == 'policy'. direction='out_depends_on'. Deduplicate by urn. Truncate to first 5 entries. Missing if target_action is MissingSlot OR if the resolved action has no outbound depends_on edges to policy entities. NOTE: 'permission model' from scope §9.4 folds into the union of preconditions (the policy-kind subset there) AND governing_policies (the depends_on path) — both edge types encode permission/governance binding, kept as separate slots so authors can render them differently (preconditions = 'must hold first', governing_policies = 'rules that bind the action's behavior').

slots.name: expected_effects
slots.derivation_rule: List of {urn, name, kind, edge_type, direction} entries describing what the resolved action produces or modifies as side effects. Walk three outbound edge types from target_action.urn: (a) 'produces' edges — typically state-kind targets (lifecycle states the action transitions to); (b) 'triggers' edges — downstream actions or UI surfaces the action invokes; (c) 'modifies' edges — typically object-kind targets (data the action mutates). Each entry's edge_type names which path produced it; direction='out_produces' / 'out_triggers' / 'out_modifies' respectively. Deduplicate by urn (first edge_type encountered wins). Truncate to first 5 entries. Missing if target_action is MissingSlot OR if the resolved action has none of these outbound edge types.

slots.name: safe_alternatives
slots.derivation_rule: List of {urn, name, kind, action_verb} sibling actions sharing the resolved action's element.object value (the canonical 'safe alternatives on the same object' pattern: cancel/renew on Subscription, retry/capture on PaymentAuthorization). Query the entities table for action-kind entities where element.object equals target_action.object AND urn != target_action.urn. action_verb is target.element.action (or target.element.name when element.action is unset, mirroring semantic_location's primary_action self_action fallback). Truncate to first 5 entries. Missing if target_action is MissingSlot OR if target_action.object is empty/null (the corpus's action-submit-order has empty element.object — no sibling-by-object lookup is possible) OR if no other action shares the object value. The safe-alternatives slot is intentionally permissive: reporting empty alternates is informative (a singleton action on an object), so the MissingSlot reason names which precondition failed (no object value, vs no siblings under that object).
